A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Paper2Rebuttal/RebuttalAgent. Their complete text, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison. Existing prompts and case studies can be matched across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original RebuttalBench comparisons and component ablations in Tables 1–2, plus generated-response case studies in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds human annotation, author evaluation, alternate-judge evaluation, additional baseline results, and qualitative analyses in Appendices D–G.

M1.justification: The Rebuttal Letter Writer prompt changes its missing-experiment rule: v1 Appendix D requires invented plausible numbers marked with an asterisk; v2 Appendix H prohibits fabrication and requires [TBD]. This changes the specified drafting procedure while retaining the architecture. However, the following rule still refers to speculative, asterisk-marked data. The PDFs do not establish whether existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds a supplementary evaluation on recent CVPR 2026 submissions, comprising 33 review-comment cases assessed by nine authors. This extends the represented manuscripts and evaluation population beyond the retained ICLR 2023 benchmark, while preserving the rebuttal-generation task. Annotation of the existing 106 benchmark cases does not constitute additional dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v1 compares against direct-to-text outputs from four model backbones. v2 retains these comparisons and adds standard RAG, AutoGen, and Jiu-Jitsu in Appendix F/Table 7, all using Gemini3-Flash. These introduce retrieval-based, general multi-agent, and prior rebuttal-specific comparators, substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include blind human annotation of 106 cases, an author study comparing four systems on 33 cases using three 1–5 rating dimensions, and rescoring Gemini-generated outputs with GPT-5-mini instead of the default Gemini judge. Appendix E also introduces a BLEU-4/ROUGE-L case comparison. The original main evaluation protocol and nine-component rubric remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds validation of outcome labels and confidence tiers, human–automated evaluation agreement, judge-model robustness, a case examining overlap-metric limitations, and a checker case investigating inflated coverage from verbose responses. These are substantial new analyses of benchmark reliability and system behavior. The original component ablations and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E introduces statistical association estimation through Kendall rank correlation between human and automated scores, reporting tau = 0.646. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the system comparisons; the new assertions of statistical validation are not accompanied by uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 are unchanged, but Tables 3–7 add substantial results. Examples include reported 100% outcome-label accuracy, alternate-judge averages of 3.84 versus 4.13, and human faithfulness scores of 2.88 versus 4.33 for Gemini and RebuttalAgent-Gemini. Table 7 reports RAG 3.11, Jiu-Jitsu 1.42, and AutoGen 3.56 against RebuttalAgent 4.23. These are newly reported comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: The score-aggregation equations and existing mathematical case-study content are retained. The added discussions of information-theoretic arguments and Utility/Reward clarification describe illustrative rebuttal cases; they introduce no developed theorem, proof, or formal analysis of RebuttalAgent.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: evidence-centric rebuttal planning, concern-conditioned evidence construction, inspectable verification, and RebuttalBench evaluation. Additional experiments support these existing claims without materially redefining their scope or novelty.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of the checker's coverage/constructiveness tradeoff, interpretations supporting human-aligned judging and criticizing overlap metrics, and explanations of comparator weaknesses. New limitations address latency, cost, incomplete artifact reuse, and venue conventions; an ethics section discusses misleading responses and confidentiality. Some interpretations overreach, notably the zero-leakage claim despite Table 3 showing Tier 3 cases classified as Tier 1.

D1.justification: Appendix D expands documentation of filtering priorities, confidence tiers, ambiguous-case handling, and the 106-case benchmark count; it does not establish that the benchmark was resampled. v2 also identifies the RAG embedding model as all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and documents new study procedures. The abstract's code-release promise is removed, while the project and demo links remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds five references, including Kendall's rank-correlation paper and VBench++, primarily around the new evaluation discussion. Appendix F adds explicit positioning against RAG, AutoGen, and Jiu-Jitsu. The main related-work sections remain substantially unchanged; the LED-merging publication update is bibliographic rather than a new cited work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order are retained. Changes include local wording and naming edits, removal of a duplicated filtering sentence, new limitations/ethics sections, and insertion of Appendices D–G. Existing prompt templates and case studies move from Appendices D/E to H/I without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds five substantive tables: an annotation confusion matrix, alternate-judge results, human-study scores, corresponding automated scores, and expanded baseline comparisons. Figures 1–3 and the original Tables 1–2 retain their content and basic presentation. Existing boxed prompts and case studies are retained with page reflow.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical case relies on an unvalidated single LLM judge and direct-to-text baselines. v2 substantially strengthens that foundation through actual-author evaluation, alternate-judge checks, and RAG/AutoGen/Jiu-Jitsu comparisons. The drafting-rule correction also addresses an important conflict with the paper's faithfulness goal. These gains outweigh material remaining flaws: the prompt still mentions speculative asterisk-marked data, and Table 3 contradicts the claimed zero tier leakage by showing 2/6 human Tier 3 cases assigned Tier 1. The revision provides substantially better evidence, although its strongest reliability claims remain overstated.
